Rashi on Nazir 4b:10:1.hebrew: מרבה אני חטאת ואשם שכן מתפיסן בנדר - שאינו מביא חטאת ואשם עד שיהא מחויב להן, ויאמר: "זהו לחטאתי ולאשמי":
Rashi on Nazir 4b:10:1.english: I include a sin-offering and a guilt-offering, as one consecrates them through a vow - For one does not bring a sin-offering or a guilt-offering until he is obligated in them and says: 'This is for my sin-offering,' or: '[This is] for my guilt-offering.'

Rashi on Nazir 4b:10:2.hebrew: שאין מתפיסו את הבכור בנדר - דנדור ועומד מרחם הוא. אבל גבי נזיר, דכו"ע — בין לר' יעקב בין לר' יוסי — בעינן דבר הנדור, וכי אמר ״הריני נזיר שמשון״, לא אמר ולא כלום:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:10:2.english: As one does not grant the firstborn consecrated status by means of a vow - For it already stands consecrated from the womb. But with regard to a nazirite, everyone agrees — both according to Rabbi Ya’akov and according to Rabbi Yosei — that we require an item [forbidden by] a vow; and if one said, “I am hereby a Samsonite nazirite,” he has said nothing at all.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:13:1.hebrew: גבי נזיר נמי - בין לר' יעקב בין לרבי יוסי, אמאי בעינן דבר הנדור? הא כתיב ביה: "לה' להזיר":
Rashi on Nazir 4b:13:1.english: With regard to a nazirite as well - Whether according to Rabbi Ya’akov or according to Rabbi Yosei, why do we require an item forbidden by a vow? Isn’t it written regarding it: “To the Lord, to consecrate himself”?

Rashi on Nazir 4b:14:1.hebrew: לא אכלתי [אשם] נזירות מעולם - משום ההוא טעמא דאמרי' לעיל, דכשהן מטמאין ורבין עליהן ימי טומאה, הן מתחרטין ומביאין חולין לעזרה:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:14:1.english: I never ate [the guilt-offering of] a nazirite - Because of that reason that we said above: that when they become ritually impure and the days of ritual impurity multiply upon them, they regret [their vow] and bring unconsecrated [animals] to the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:15:1.english: And rushed - And my [evil] inclination rushed upon me and brought me to [sinful] thoughts.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:15:2.hebrew: לשאוב מים מן הגיע גרסי' - שכן הוא לשון המשנה, ופי' מן המעיין:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:15:2.english: “To draw water from the hagia” is the reading - For such is the language of the Mishnah, and its meaning is: “From the spring.”

Rashi on Nazir 4b:16:1.english: With regard to you the verse states: “When a man clearly utters a vow, the vow of a nazirite, to consecrate himself to the Lord” - Which implies that one vows for the sake of Heaven.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:17:1.hebrew: ושמשון לאו נזיר הוא והא כתיב כי נזיר אלהים - וקא ס"ד דמנוח קאמר להא מילתא, דהוה ליה דבר הנדור, דאדם מדיר את בנו בנזיר:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:17:1.english: And was Samson not a nazirite? But isn’t it written: “For a nazirite of God…” - And it entered [the Gemara’s] mind that Manoah said this statement, so that it would be a matter [effected by a] vow, as a person may vow for his son to be a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:17:2.hebrew: מלאך הוא דקאמר - כי נזיר אלהים יהיה הנער מן הבטן, אבל מפי מנוח לא יצא:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:17:2.english: It was the angel who said [it] - “For the child shall be a nazirite of God from the womb,” but it did not issue from the mouth of Manoah.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:18:1.hebrew: דילמא גרדויי גרד להו - מחתך חתך בהן, אבל הוא גופיה לא נגע בהו:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:18:1.english: Perhaps he slashed them - He cut into them, but he himself did not touch them.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:19:1.english: “And he smote… and took” is written - Which implies that he smote [them], and then he took [their garments].

Rashi on Nazir 4b:20:1.hebrew: גוססין שוינהו - ובהדי דהוו גוססין, אשלחינהו, ולא איטמי בהו:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:20:1.english: He made them moribund - And while they were moribund, he stripped them [of their garments], and did not become defiled by them.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:21:1.english: And where is a permanent nazirite written - [That is, one] who lightens [his hair] with a razor and brings three animal [offerings].

Rashi on Nazir 4b:21:2.hebrew: ה"ג דתניא רבי אומר אבשלום נזיר עולם היה שנאמר ויהי מקץ ארבעים שנה ומגלח היה אבשלום לשנים עשר חדש - דבכך הוה ליה כובד, ובבציר מהכי לא ה"ל כובד, דכאיש גבורתו (שופטים ח). אבל שאר נזירי עולם מגלח א' לל' יום, דהוי ליה בהכי כובד:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:21:2.english: This is the reading: “As it is taught: Rabbi says: Absalom was a permanent nazirite, as it is stated: ‘And it came to pass at the end of forty years,’ and Absalom would cut [his hair] once every twelve months” - For with that [period], he experienced heaviness [of hair], and with less than this, he did not experience heaviness, for “as a man is, so is his strength” (Judges 8:21). But other permanent nazirites cut [their hair] once every thirty days, as they experience heaviness with that [amount].

Rashi on Nazir 4b:4:1.hebrew: מני אי רבי יהודה הא אמר דמותר לכתחילה - ליטמא, ומתני' קתני: ״אם נטמא״ — בדיעבד, אבל לכתחילה לא:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:4:1.english: Whose [opinion is it]? If Rabbi Yehuda, didn't he say that it is permitted ab initio - To become impure; and the mishna teaches: "If he becomes impure" — [which implies] after the fact, but ab initio, no.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:5:1.english: [The tanna] also taught with regard to a nazirite like Samson: "If" - And the same law applies: even ab initio it is permitted.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:6:1.english: [It is] hereby upon me - This loaf [is] like a firstborn.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:6:2.hebrew: רבי יעקב אוסר - דלא בעינן שיהא איסורו בדבר הנידר, כגון (חטאת) ושלמים (דהא כתיב: ״איש כי ידור נדר לה'״, לרבות דבר האסור, כגון בכור):
Rashi on Nazir 4b:6:2.english: Rabbi Ya’akov prohibits - For we do not require that its prohibition be through an item prohibited by a vow, such as (a sin offering) and peace offerings (for behold, it is written: "When a man vows a vow to the Lord" — to include an item forbidden [by Heaven], such as a firstborn).

Rashi on Nazir 4b:7:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה סבר לה כר' יעקב דאמר לא בעינן דבר הנדור - הכי נמי, כי אמר הריני נזיר שמשון הוי נזיר, ואע"ג דשמשון לא יצא נזירות מפיו:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:7:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds in accordance with Rabbi Ya’akov, who said [that] we do not require an item rendered forbidden by a vow - So too, when one says: “I am hereby a nazirite like Samson,” he becomes a nazirite, even though regarding Samson, naziriteship did not issue from his mouth.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:7:2.hebrew: ור"ש - דאומר לא הוי נזיר, סבר לה כר' יוסי, דאמר מותר, משום דלא התפיס אלא בבכור, דלא הוי דבר הנדור, שהרי קדושתו מרחם:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:7:2.english: And Rabbi Shimon - Who says [that] he does not become a nazirite, holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who said [that it is] permitted, because he only associated [it] with a firstborn, which is not an item rendered forbidden by a vow, for its sanctity is from the womb.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:8:1.hebrew: ושאני גבי בכור - דהיינו טעמא דרבי יעקב, משום דכתיב ״לה'״ — ״איש כי ידור נדר לה'״ — לרבות את הבכור:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:8:1.english: And it is different with regard to a firstborn - That is the reasoning of Rabbi Ya’akov: because it is written “to the Lord” — “When a man vows a vow to the Lord” [Numbers 30:3] — to include the firstborn.

Rashi on Nazir 4b:9:1.hebrew: לרבות חטאת ואשם - דכי אמר: ״ככר זה עלי כחטאת וכאשם״, אסור:
Rashi on Nazir 4b:9:1.english: To include a sin-offering and a guilt-offering - That if one says: “This loaf is [forbidden] to me like a sin-offering and like a guilt-offering,” it is forbidden.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:12:1.hebrew: שמצוה לקדש - פירוש: "בכור תקדיש", ולומר: "תוקדש בבכורה", אע"פ דקדיש מרחם:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:12:1.english: "That there is a mitzvah to consecrate [it]" - Explanation: "[Regarding a] firstborn, you shall consecrate [it]" (Deuteronomy 15:19) — and [this means] to say, "May it be consecrated as a firstborn," even though it is consecrated from the womb.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:12:2.hebrew: מי לא קדוש - הלכך לאו דבר הנדור הוא, כיון דאינו אלא מצוה בעלמא:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:12:2.english: "Is it not consecrated?" - Therefore, it is not an item forbidden by a vow, since [consecrating it] is merely a mitzvah.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:13:1.hebrew: גבי נזיר נמי הכתיב לה' - וכי היכי דמרבי ר' יעקב בכור מלה', ה"נ נרבה נזיר שמשון מלה' דכתי' בנזיר:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:13:1.english: "With regard to a nazirite as well, isn't it written: 'to the Lord'" - And just as Rabbi Ya'akov includes a firstborn from "to the Lord," so too, let us include a Samson nazirite from "to the Lord" that is written regarding a nazirite.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:14:1.hebrew: לא אכלתי אשם נזירות - אבל שאר אשמות היה אוכל; אבל אשם נזיר היה קשה בעיניו לאוכלו, לפי שאינו בא אלא בנזיר שנטמא. וכיון שנטמא, הי' דואג פן מתחרט על נדרו, שהימים הראשונים נופלין, ומביא חולין בעזרה:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:14:1.english: "I never ate the guilt-offering of naziriteship" - However, he would eat other guilt-offerings; but as for the guilt-offering of a nazirite, he was reluctant to eat it, since it is brought only for a nazirite who became ritually impure. And since he became ritually impure, [Shimon HaTzaddik] was concerned lest [the nazirite] regret his vow — since the initial days fall away — and [thereby] bring non-consecrated [animals] into the Temple courtyard.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:16:1.hebrew: עליך הכתוב אומר להזיר לה' - כלומר: שתחילת נדרו לגמרי לש"ש, ולא היה דואג שיתחרט, אע"פ שנטמא. אבל שאר נודרים — סתמא נודרי' בעת צרה או על עבירה שבידן, כדי להצטער ולכפר על עונם; וכשמתרבים הימים עליהם ממה שגמרו בדעתן, קרוב להיות תוהא על הראשונות:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:16:1.english: "With regard to you the verse states: 'To consecrate himself to the Lord'" - That is to say, the beginning of his vow was completely for the sake of Heaven, and [Shimon HaTzaddik] was not concerned that he would regret [his vow], even though he became ritually impure. However, other people who vow typically vow in a time of distress, or on account of a sin they have committed, in order to afflict themselves and atone for their sin; and when the days multiply upon them beyond what they had resolved in their minds, it is likely that [such a person] will come to regret the original [vow].

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:17:1.hebrew: שמשון לאו נדור הוה - פירוש: לא נדור נזיר הוה? והא כתיב: "כי נזיר אלהים יהיה" כו'. וקס"ד שהמלאך היה אומר לאביו שיזירנו לכשיולד, כדאמרי' לקמן (נזיר דף כח:): "האיש מדיר בנו בנזיר":
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:17:1.english: "Was Samson not vowed" - Explanation: Was he not a vowed nazirite? For isn't it written: "For the child shall be a nazirite of God..."? And [the Gemara] initially thought that the angel was telling his father to vow him as a nazirite once he was born, as we say below (Nazir 28b): "A man may vow his son as a nazirite."

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:17:2.hebrew: התם מלאך הוא דקאמר ליה - בנבואה, ולא יצא נזירות לא מפי אביו ולא מפי שמשון:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:17:2.english: "There, it was an angel who said to him" - [This was] through prophecy, and [the] naziriteship did not issue either from his father's mouth or from Samson's mouth.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:18:1.hebrew: גרויי גרי - לשון חצים, כלומר: מרחוק זורק בהם והרגם:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:18:1.english: Garoyei gari - An expression of arrows [girei]; that is to say, from a distance he threw [the jawbone] at them and killed them.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:20:1.hebrew: דילמא גוססין שווינהו - לאו דוקא גוססים, כי נזיר אסור ליגע לגוסס; אלא כלומר: קרוב לגוססין:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:20:1.english: "Perhaps he made them moribund" - [This does] not literally mean moribund, because a Nazirite is forbidden to touch a moribund person; rather, it means: close to [being] moribund.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:20:2.hebrew: אלא גמר' - פירוש: דגמרי' דקטלינהו ממש, והדר שלוחי שלחינן. ואפי' למאן דאמר (יבמות סא.): "קברי עובדי כוכבים אינן מטמאין באהל" — במגע מיהא מטמאין:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:20:2.english: "Rather, it is learned as a tradition" - Explanation: It is learned by tradition that he actually killed them, and afterward stripped them [of their garments]. And even according to the one who says (Yevamot 61a): "The graves of gentiles do not impart impurity in a tent" — at any rate, through contact they do impart impurity.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:21:1.hebrew: ונזיר עולם היכא כתיב - כלומר: שמותר להקל; ומייתי מאבשלום שהיה מיקל, למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:21:1.english: "And where is a permanent nazirite written?" - That is to say: [Where is it written] that he is permitted to lighten [his hair]? And [the Gemara] brings [proof] from Absalom, who would lighten [his hair], each Master according to his [own view].

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:21:2.hebrew: את נדרי אשר נדרתי - וסתם נדר משמע ליה נזירות. ועוד: אחר שלא היה מגלח אלא מימים לימים, משמע שהכביד עליו שערו — מכלל דנזירות נדר:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:21:2.english: “My vow, which I have vowed” - And an unspecified vow implied nezirut to him [Rabbi]. And furthermore: since he did not cut [his hair] except from year to year, which indicates that his hair had grown heavy upon him, it follows that it was nezirut that he vowed.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:2:1.hebrew: קרבן הוא דלא מייתי - פירוש: נזיר שמשון. אבל נזירות חייל עליה — כלומר, לענין שאסור לטמאות למתים לכתחילה:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:2:1.english: "It is an offering that he does not bring" - Explanation: [This refers to] a nazirite like Samson. "However, naziriteship applies to him" — that is to say, with regard to the matter that it is forbidden to become impure from a corpse ab initio.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:3:1.hebrew: שלא מצינו בשמשון שיצא נזירות מפיו - כלומר: לא נזר בנזיר, אלא מבטן אמו היה נדור בנזיר ממילא. ואנן בעינן שידור בדבר הנדור, כמו "הריני כזה שנדר בנזיר", כדדרשי' (נדרים דף יד.): "כי ידור נדר" — עד שידור בדבר הנדור:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:3:1.english: "Since we do not find with Samson that naziriteship left his mouth" - That is to say, he did not take a nazirite vow; rather, from his mother's womb he was bound as a nazirite automatically. And we require that one vow by [associating with] something prohibited by a vow, such as [one who says], "I hereby become like this [person] who took a nazirite vow," as we expound (Nedarim 14a): "'When [a man] vows a vow' — until he vows by [associating with] something prohibited by a vow."

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:6:1.english: "It is hereby upon me like a firstborn" - Explanation: "This loaf is like a firstborn."

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:8:1.hebrew: לא דכ"ע - כלומר: כ"ע, אי אמר "כעולה וכשלמים", הוי דבר הנדור; אבל בכור קדוש מרחם אמו. רבי יהודה סבר לה כרבי יעקב, דאמר לא בעינן דבר הנדור; ואם אמר "הריני כשמשון" הוי נזיר — אע"ג דנזיר שמשון לאו נדור הוה, אלא קדוש מבטן אמו, כבכור:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:8:1.english: "No, that everyone [agrees]" - That is to say: Everyone [agrees that] if one said, "[This is to me] like a burnt offering" or "like a peace offering," it is an item forbidden by a vow; but a firstborn is sacred from its mother's womb. [The Gemara had therefore suggested that] Rabbi Yehuda holds in accordance with Rabbi Ya'akov, who said that we do not require an item forbidden by a vow; and [consequently,] if one said, "I am hereby like Samson," he becomes a nazirite, even though Samson's naziriteship was not [established by] a vow, but rather he was sacred from his mother's womb, like a firstborn.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:8:2.hebrew: לא דכ"ע בעינן דבר הנדור בעלמא לגבי נזירות ושאני הכא דכתיב לה' - "כי ידור נדר לה'" — לרבות את הבכור. כלומר: שהוא לה' ממילא, אפילו [הכי] הוי נדור:
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:8:2.english: "No, everyone [agrees that] we require an item forbidden by a vow in general regarding naziriteship, and it is different here, as it is written: 'To the Lord'" - "[When a man] vows a vow to the Lord" (Numbers 30:3) — [this comes] to include the firstborn. That is to say, [even though] it belongs to the Lord automatically, even so it is [considered] an item forbidden by a vow.

Tosafot on Nazir 4b:9:1.hebrew: לרבות את החטאת ואשם - דסד"א: עולה ושלמים הבאים נדבה הוי דבר הנדור, אבל בחטאת ואשם הבאים בחובה לא מיקרי דבר הנדור — קמ"ל "לה'", דמרבי כל מילי דהוי לה':
Tosafot on Nazir 4b:9:1.english: "To include a sin-offering and a guilt-offering" - For you might have thought: A burnt-offering and peace-offerings, which are brought voluntarily, are an item forbidden by a vow; but regarding a sin-offering and a guilt-offering, which are brought as an obligation, they are not called an item forbidden by a vow. [Therefore, the verse] teaches us: "To the Lord," which includes anything that is [dedicated] to the Lord.
